chapter: Duke, Gensel and the later years
title: Organizing a big band for Reverend Gensel's church
summary: McGhee starts a big band for Sunday Vespers at St. Peter's, and band members hit Gensel for money.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: So in this period, you were finished with the group of Phil Porter, you were doing things here and there, and then you started with Gensel in that period?

Yeah. Well, I told the Reverend I wanted to organize a big band to play for the church, so that, you know, it would draw some people over there. I knew that would do it, especially if it's a swinging band.
Had he been transferred to St. Peter's by this time?

No, but he was being transferred at that time we was talking about. He'd invite the faculty up to his house, and so forth and so on. So they decided to give him the job as the man at St. Peter's, to control the Vespers services and so forth.

So I got to organize the band, and we started rehearsing over at the Church. Then you know how it is with guys in the band. If they think they can get some money, they always want some money. So I didn't pay no mind, because I wasn't thinking about asking them for no money, but I figured with the influence of what I was doing, it would carry me through whatever would come out of it, you know. Which it did, in a sense. But I didn't know that the guys was hittin' Reverend Gensel for bread. They went behind my back, and I didn't know it. So I thought that was kind of dirty, because they never told me, said, "Well,

look, Maggie, you'd better get you a taste, man, because you know, this guy's giving away bread." And the Reverend Gensel never offered nothing, so I just went along with the program that everything was cool. We was just working stuff out together. But I didn't know that he was giving money to the band all the time. Like, guys would come up to him and say, "I need a dollar or two for transportation" or whatever they needed the money for, and they'd give him some story, and you know, he'd give them...

When I found out about it, I said, "John, I hear you're giving money to the band." He says, "Yeah, I have to. They're always asking me for money, so I give them some." I said, "Well, don't be doing that on me. That's not okay. Then you don't know where the money is going." And he had gotten the gig over at the church at this time, and we were playing there every Sunday damn near.

Yeah, for the Vespers. Which was good, because at least it gave us something to do, and it gave me something to do, because I had to write a lot of music to keep the band sound and fresh and everything. It took a little while for that to happen, but I did the best I could. We got an album date out of it anyway.
